title: Capacity maxed out
summary: Every scheduler busy and the storage at its cap at the same time. CPU sessions run back-to-back CPU-heavy reports at MAXDOP 1, one scheduler each, more sessions than schedulers (on Azure SQL Database, CPU at the vCore limit). IO sessions scan and update a scratch set (shared with io-pressure) that the first one grows to scratchMb after a free-space check, so reads miss the buffer pool once it's bigger than memory. Business data is only read.

concurrency.description: CPU sessions; T1 and T2 have 2 vCPUs and T3 at most 1 vCore, so 8 keeps every scheduler busy with several runnable tasks each.

intensity.description: CPU work per report and the pause between units of work: about 1 second at 1, none at 10.

notes.T1: The ContosoCare data file sits on the VM's managed disk (the OS disk in lowest-cost, a data disk otherwise) with its IOPS and throughput caps; the 16 GB data cap leaves room for the default 6 GB scratch set, and the runner checks free space first.
notes.T2: The guest's VHDX sits on the host's disk; the 8 GB data cap keeps the default scratch set at 4 GB with a 512 MB margin.
notes.T3: CPU at the serverless maximum vCores and reads governed by the service objective (IO stalls queued by resource governance).

ioWorkers.description: Sessions scanning and updating the scratch set (0 for CPU only).

scratchMb.description: Size of the scratch data set in MB, shared with io-pressure. Reads become physical once it no longer fits in the buffer pool.

expectedHubSignals.signal: SqlServerCPUUtilization: SQLProcessCPUPercent (SQL Server) or AvgCPUPercent (Azure SQL Database, of the vCore limit) at or near 100
SqlServerWaitStats: CPU wait category (SOS_SCHEDULER_YIELD) and signal waits from runnable tasks
SqlServerWaitStats: Buffer IO wait category (PAGEIOLATCH_SH) once the scratch set exceeds memory
SqlServerStorageIO: IO stalls on the ContosoCare data file at the disk's caps; on Azure SQL Database, IOStallQueuedReadMs from IO governance

expectedSymptoms: CPU pinned near 100% with every scheduler busy and several runnable tasks each
Read IO at the disk's IOPS or throughput cap, with rising read latency
Everything else on the target slows down: the healthy baseline's requests take longer
queryLevelEvidence: sys.dm_os_schedulers: runnable_tasks_count above 0 on every scheduler (needs VIEW SERVER STATE)
sys.dm_io_virtual_file_stats for the ContosoCare data file, or sys.dm_db_resource_stats on Azure SQL Database
reset: Auto-cleanup and reset truncate demo.io_scratch when no io-pressure or capacity-max run still uses it; the space stays allocated for the next run, and business data is only read.
